assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology to incretin-based therapy is a rare complete arc from hormone biology to drugs that treat type 2 diabetes and obesity and show cardiovascular, renal and other organ benefits; the clinical and societal impact is very large and the discovery is clear.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology, GLP-1 as the active form), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinotrophic GLP-2, translational work) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis) are the most defensible trio from the supplied names; Knudsen is key to liraglutide/semaglutide development but is more a drug-development contribution, and Habener is not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism and efficacy are confirmed in multiple large independent outcome trials over more than a decade; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the first characterization of the active GLP-1 peptide is contested and I cannot verify the details from memory.
Whether the prize should reward physiology or the drug development (Knudsen) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells delivering durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies changed cancer therapy and opened a new therapeutic modality; the concept is original and the impact on patients is striking.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation) and June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL and ALL) are the strongest pairing; Rosenberg's TIL and early gene-modified T-cell work is relevant but a distinct line, and Eshhar (originator of the chimeric receptor concept) is not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long-term follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers; solid tumors, toxicity and cost remain open but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Omission of Eshhar from the supplied credit weakens a fair allocation.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity and is a methodological revolution used across fields, with early clinical applications in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its demonstration as a neuronal tool (Deisseroth, Boyden, with Miesenböck's earlier genetic light-control work) make a three-person limit hard; this trio is my best compromise but excludes Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and mature for more than a decade; recognition is timely, with a tool-versus-disease-discovery question for a medicine prize.
uncertainties: Six credited names cannot be fairly reduced to three.
Therapeutic benefit so far is limited and the prize is mainly for a research tool.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS, cGAMP and STING is a fundamental innate immunity pathway central to antiviral defense, autoinflammatory interferonopathies, autoimmunity and tumor immunity; it is conceptually clear and of broad relevance, including to my own field of interferon-driven autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber identified STING; Ishikawa co-described STING with Barber, and Sun and Wu were first authors in Chen's lab. Two laureates is the cleanest pairing; the Vance, Patel and Carlson contributions of cyclic-dinucleotide biochemistry are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in genetics (STING-associated vasculopathy, Aicardi-Goutieres) and many labs; therapeutic modulators are still in trials, so clinical translation is immature.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit of STING agonists or antagonists is not yet shown.
Credit among cyclic dinucleotide, STING and cGAS discoverers is shared across groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis transformed treatment of rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis, and began the biologics era for chronic inflammatory disease; the translational path from cytokine hypothesis to patients is exemplary.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the cytokine-network studies and the first anti-TNF clinical trials; the supplied credit supports a fair two-person prize, though antibody engineering (e.g. Vilcek, Cerami) and cytokine discovery have other claimants not listed here.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of clinical experience with several agents confirms efficacy and safety profile; recognition is not premature and arguably long overdue.
uncertainties: The prize might be perceived as favoring a rheumatology-related topic; I assess it on the merits and apply the shared conflict protocol.
Allocation relative to TNF discovery and antibody-engineering contributions is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cell survival, not only proliferation, drives cancer and defined the apoptosis regulatory machinery; this led to venetoclax and BH3 mimetics, a mechanism-to-drug success.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterized the translocated BCL2 gene and the BCL-2 family; Vaux showed with Cory that BCL-2 acts as a survival factor cooperating with MYC; Strasser is a major later contributor. Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer (the original t(14;18) cloning, one deceased) and Horvitz's ced-9 link complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with clinical validation in CLL and AML and robust confirmation of mechanism over three decades.
uncertainties: The apoptosis field already received a prize in 2002, so novelty relative to that award is a question.
Priority of the t(14;18) BCL2 cloning among several groups is disputed in my recollection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level reductions in high-grade lesions and cervical cancer demonstrated; this is a major preventive medicine achievement building on the 2008 HPV prize.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs; Frazer (with Zhou) developed the VLP approach in parallel, and Koutsky and others contributed to trials; the supplied trio is plausible but Jian Zhou, deceased, is not credited and priority between groups is debated.
assessment.maturity: Population data from Sweden, Scotland and elsewhere confirm effectiveness; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2008 award for HPV and cervical cancer may reduce prize appeal.
Priority among the VLP groups is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PCSK9 combined human genetics (gain- and loss-of-function variants) with a new biology of LDL receptor degradation to produce a validated target and a new class of potent LDL-lowering drugs with outcome benefit; it is a model of genetics-guided drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Abifadel and Boileau first reported PCSK9 gain-of-function mutations in hypercholesterolemia; Seidah identified and characterized PCSK9; Hobbs and Cohen showed loss-of-function variants lower LDL and coronary risk. Five credited names exceed the prize limit, and any three omit decisive contributors.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by outcome trials of antibodies and siRNA; the field is mature enough but the statin precedent makes novelty of the impact partly incremental.
uncertainties: Allocation among genetic discovery, biochemistry and population genetics is difficult.
Impact is on a risk factor that statins already treat for many patients.
